claim: Forecast-model performance is task- and dataset-dependent; no single model dominates all TestReal and Fresh WildBox conditions.
basis: Paired track-cluster bootstrap shows mixed directions and significance patterns across horizons/datasets.

claim: The frozen Transformer ensemble is the overall best forecasting model.
basis: On BIRDSAI TestReal 2s→2s, Transformer has significantly higher ADE/FDE than GRU and LSTM; on 2s→5s it is significantly worse than GRU.

claim: On BIRDSAI TestReal, Transformer clearly improves over constant-velocity forecasting at both 2s and 5s horizons.
basis: Track-cluster 95% CIs for Transformer − ConstantVelocity are below zero for ADE and FDE at both horizons.

claim: On Fresh WildBox 2s→2s, Transformer improves ADE over Stationary, ConstantVelocity and KalmanCV, but is not clearly different from GRU/LSTM.
basis: Track-cluster ADE CIs exclude zero versus Stationary/CV/KalmanCV, but include zero versus GRU/LSTM; only 10 tracks.

claim: On Fresh WildBox 2s→5s, Transformer FDE is slightly lower than GRU/LSTM, but ADE differences versus GRU/LSTM are uncertain.
basis: Track-cluster FDE CIs are narrowly below zero versus GRU/LSTM; ADE CIs include zero; only 10 tracks.

claim: LSTM outperforms GRU on BIRDSAI TestReal 2s→2s, but their differences are uncertain for TestReal 2s→5s and Fresh WildBox.
basis: Paired track-cluster LSTM−GRU CIs are below zero only for TestReal 2s→2s ADE/FDE.

claim: Track-cluster bootstrap is the primary inferential analysis; source-cluster bootstrap is sensitivity analysis only.
basis: Source counts are small, especially Fresh WildBox with only 3 sources, so source-level intervals are too coarse for primary claims.

claim: Transformer superiority is statistically established across datasets.
basis: Multiple comparisons are uncertain or favor recurrent models; there is no cross-condition dominance.
